subject: MAP: success SLIs, exit gates & acceptance tests
messages:
From: Emily Wong <emily@healthmetrics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Patel <amit@healthmetrics.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — acceptance criteria request

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at HealthMetrics came away excited. Before we lock timelines with Procurement, they asked for a concrete acceptance checklist we can share with internal stakeholders (data ops, security, and platform). Specifically:

- A short list of SLIs we can show engineering (latency/throughput/accuracy).
- The minimum acceptance tests to run during the 2-week evaluation window.
- The decision tree for accept / partial-accept / rollback.

Can you send a one-pager or spreadsheet with tests (inputs, expected outputs, pass thresholds) and owners? We want to avoid vague terms like "works well" for the legal review.

If you have a sample harness or a couple test cases we can run on our side (non-prod), that would speed things up.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Wong
Director of Engineering, HealthMetrics
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Wong <emily@healthmetrics.com>, Amit Patel <amit@healthmetrics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — acceptance criteria request

Emily — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a first-pass MAP workbook (MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short spec for the acceptance-test harness (acceptance-test-harness-spec.md). High-level summary below so your stakeholders can scan quickly.

1) Success SLIs (primary — must pass to be "Accepted")
  - Latency: p95 inference latency <= 600ms for 2k-token requests during 95th percentile of evaluation load
  - Availability: >= 99.5% during the evaluation window (excluding agreed maintenance windows)
  - Functional concordance: classification/concordance >= 92% on the provided gold set (see tests below)
  - Semantic recall: embedding-based retrieval recall >= 90% (top-5) on the sample corpus

2) Secondary QoS checks (informational; failure here triggers discussion, not automatic rollback)
  - Throughput: sustained 120 requests/min with no error spikes
  - Token-cost variance: invoice tokens within +/-10% of forecasted run rate
  - Drift: embedding similarity distribution shift <= 3% vs baseline

3) Acceptance tests (minimal set to run during 14-day eval)
  - Smoke test (Day 0): basic end-to-end generation and embedding retrieval on 12 representative queries. Pass if no functional regressions and latencies below 1s.
  - Regression suite (Day 2–5): run prefabricated 200-case test set (attached). Pass threshold: concordance >= 92%.
  - Load test (Day 6): ramp to target throughput (120 req/min) for 1 hour; monitor p95 and error rate.
  - Security checklist (parallel): SOC2 evidence review + network connectivity test egress rules.

4) Exit gates / decision tree
  - Accept: All primary SLIs passed + security checklist satisfied + sign-off from HealthMetrics Eng and Security (POC owners).
  - Conditional Accept: One primary SLI missed by <= 5% but a remediation plan with patch timeline <= 7 business days + acceptance of temporary SLA credit.
  - Reject / Rollback: Any primary SLI missed by > 5% or security evidence gaps not remediated within 5 business days.

5) Owners & timeline
  - Redwood deliverable: test harness + support during load run (owner: Rafael) — delivery within 48 hours of kickoff.
  - HealthMetrics owners: Eng lead to run regression suite; Security to confirm SOC2 copy; Procurement to issue PO.
  - Acceptance window: 14 calendar days starting on the day Redwood hands over the harness and test data.

Attachments referenced in the workbook include concrete test inputs and expected output examples. Link to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cMAP-HealthMetrics

Next steps: I can (1) schedule a 30-minute run-through of the workbook and harness with your Eng lead, or (2) drop the test harness and let you run it asynchronously. Which do you prefer?

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Wong <emily@healthmetrics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: success SLIs, exit gates & acceptance tests

Adding a couple commercial & operational clarifications for HealthMetrics' procurement and legal teams:

- Acceptance period: 14 days as Rafael noted. Sign-off must be provided in writing (email) by a named HealthMetrics approver; we'll include a short acceptance form in the DocuSign packet.
- Partial acceptance credit: if we land a Conditional Accept, Redwood will provide a 10% credit for 30 days of usage while the agreed remediation is deployed.
- Evidence package: Redwood will provide a SOC2 snapshot, audit log sample (7 days), and a list of deployed model variants used in the eval. These will be attached to the MAP workbook.
- PO & SOW: Procurement should issue a PO referencing deal HM-2025-007. Attached is a PO template (po-template.docx). If legal needs redlines, loop me in — small-time changes are OK but anything material requires Legal review.

Operational note: to avoid noisy false negatives in the regression suite, please run tests against your non-prod dataset and share any preprocessing steps. Karthik will coordinate the test dataset handoff.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Amit Patel <amit@healthmetrics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: success SLIs, exit gates & acceptance tests

Thanks — this is exactly what our stakeholders needed. A few quick follow-ups from Procurement & Security:

- Can you add a short "evidence checklist" tab to the MAP_v1.xlsx that lists the exact artifact names we'll receive (SOC2.pdf, audit-log-sample.csv, harness-results.json)?
- We prefer a 14-calendar-day evaluation but would like the option to extend by up to 7 days if the load test or security review is still in progress. Is that acceptable?
- Please send the DocuSign link with the acceptance form + SOW so Procurement can start internal routing (we use an internal PO number once routed).

If you can drop the updated MAP and DocuSign envelope by EOD tomorrow, Procurement will queue the PO.

Best,
Amit Patel
Director, Platform Engineering — HealthMetrics
